llms.body:
# Centinel Analytica

> Centinel evaluates automated traffic with request, browser and session evidence, and applies your access policy.

Centinel Analytica (Centinel) is a bot protection company based in Berlin.

Centinel evaluates automated traffic and returns a policy decision for the
site's integration to apply. Available evidence and enforcement depend on the
deployment. Approved automation and abusive workflows need different policies.

## Product
- [Centinel](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/): Bot protection for websites and applications.
- [Bot management](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bot-management): What bot management covers, the controls it should provide, and how to evaluate one.
- [How it works](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/how-it-works): Follow request evidence, policy evaluation, and enforcement through the chosen integration.
- [Integrations](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/integrations): Supported stacks and rollout preparation for an evaluation.
- [Pricing](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/pricing): How to start, what drives the quote, and the procurement path. No public price list.
- [Security](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/security): Certification and programme status, which data detection processes, and how to get the data processing agreement (DPA) and policies.
- [Free AI crawler audit](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/free-audit): Get a manually reviewed report of the scraping tools that can access your content and where it is exposed.
- [Book a demo](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/book-a-demo): Book a 30-minute call with the Centinel team about your automated traffic.

## Tools
- [Tools](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/tools): The free tools, each with what it answers and where the pasted input goes.
- [Crawler IP verifier](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/verify-crawler): Checks an IP address from your logs against the reverse DNS domains and address lists that Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity publish.
- [User agent parser](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/user-agent-parser): Names the bot a user agent string claims to be, with its operator, type and robots.txt token.
- [robots.txt checker](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/robots-txt-checker): Reads a site's robots.txt and reports what it says to each AI bot, and whether the site has an llms.txt.
- [llms.txt generator](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/llms-txt-generator): Turns a sitemap or a list of page URLs into an llms.txt draft, grouped by section.

## Bot directory
- [Bot directory](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots): Each common crawler's operator, user agent, robots.txt token and verification method.
- [AI crawler list](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/ai-crawler-list): AI crawler user agents and robots.txt tokens.
- [Google crawlers](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/operator/google): The 11 Google bots in the directory, side by side.
- [OpenAI crawlers](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/operator/openai): The 3 OpenAI bots in the directory, side by side.
- [Anthropic crawlers](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/operator/anthropic): The 3 Anthropic bots in the directory, side by side.
- [Meta crawlers](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/operator/meta): The 4 Meta bots in the directory, side by side.
- [360Spider](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/360spider): 360 Search. Crawls pages for the web search of 360 Search (so.com).
- [AdsBot-Google](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/adsbot-google): Google. Checks the quality of ad landing pages for Google Ads.
- [AhrefsBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/ahrefsbot): Ahrefs. Builds the link database behind Ahrefs and the Yep search engine.
- [AhrefsSiteAudit](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/ahrefssiteaudit): Ahrefs. Crawls a site for an Ahrefs Site Audit project.
- [Amazonbot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/amazonbot): Amazon. Crawls to improve Amazon products; may be used to train Amazon AI models.
- [Applebot-Extended](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/applebot-extended): Apple. A robots.txt token that opts content out of Apple model training.
- [Applebot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/applebot): Apple. Crawls pages for Spotlight, Siri and Safari search features.
- [Baiduspider](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/baiduspider): Baidu. Crawls pages for Baidu search.
- [Barkrowler](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/barkrowler): Babbar. Collects links and page metadata for Babbar.
- [Bingbot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/bingbot): Microsoft. Crawls pages for Bing search.
- [Bytespider](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/bytespider): Unconfirmed, attributed to ByteDance. A crawler with no operator documentation.
- [CCBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/ccbot): Common Crawl. Builds Common Crawl's open web archive, free for anyone to reuse.
- [ChatGPT-User](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/chatgpt-user): OpenAI. Visits a page when a ChatGPT or Custom GPT user's request needs it.
- [Claude-SearchBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/claude-searchbot): Anthropic. Indexes pages to improve Claude's search results.
- [Claude-User](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/claude-user): Anthropic. Fetches a page when a Claude user's question needs it.
- [ClaudeBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/claudebot): Anthropic. Collects web content that could contribute to Claude model training.
- [DataForSeoBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/dataforseobot): DataForSEO. Adds links to DataForSEO's backlink database.
- [Diffbot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/diffbot): Diffbot. Crawls the web for the Diffbot Knowledge Graph and Diffbot's web search services.
- [Discordbot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/discordbot): Discord. Visits a link shared in a Discord message to build its preview.
- [DotBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/dotbot): Moz. Gathers data for the Moz Link Index.
- [DuckAssistBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/duckassistbot): DuckDuckGo. Crawls in real time to support DuckDuckGo's AI-assisted answers.
- [DuckDuckBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/duckduckbot): DuckDuckGo. Crawls pages for DuckDuckGo search.
- [facebookexternalhit](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/facebookexternalhit): Meta. Builds link previews when content is shared on Meta's apps.
- [Google-CloudVertexBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/google-cloudvertexbot): Google. Crawls sites whose owners asked for it when building Vertex AI Agents.
- [Google-Extended](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/google-extended): Google. A robots.txt token that controls Gemini training and grounding use.
- [Google-InspectionTool](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/google-inspectiontool): Google. Fetches pages for Search Console URL inspection and the Rich Results Test.
- [Googlebot-Image](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/googlebot-image): Google. Crawls images for Google Images and image features in Search.
- [Googlebot-News](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/googlebot-news): Google. Controls whether your pages appear in Google News.
- [Googlebot-Video](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/googlebot-video): Google. Crawls video for the video features of Google Search.
- [Googlebot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/googlebot): Google. Crawls pages for Google Search, Images, Video, News and Discover.
- [GoogleOther](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/googleother): Google. Fetches public pages for Google product teams, for example for research crawls.
- [GPTBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/gptbot): OpenAI. Crawls content that may be used to train OpenAI's foundation models.
- [Kagibot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/kagibot): Kagi. Crawls pages for the Kagi search engine.
- [Mediapartners-Google](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/mediapartners-google): Google. Reads the pages of sites that show Google ads, so the ads match the content.
- [Meta-ExternalAgent](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/meta-externalagent): Meta. Crawls for training AI models or improving Meta products.
- [Meta-ExternalFetcher](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/meta-externalfetcher): Meta. Fetches individual links on behalf of Meta product users.
- [Meta-WebIndexer](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/meta-webindexer): Meta. Crawls pages to improve the search results of Meta AI.
- [MistralAI-Index](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/mistralai-index): Mistral AI. Indexes pages for Mistral search.
- [MistralAI-User](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/mistralai-user): Mistral AI. Fetches a page when a Mistral user's action needs it.
- [MJ12bot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/mj12bot): Majestic. Maps links between websites for Majestic's link index.
- [OAI-SearchBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/oai-searchbot): OpenAI. Surfaces websites in ChatGPT's search features.
- [Perplexity-User](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/perplexity-user): Perplexity. Fetches a page when a Perplexity user's request needs it.
- [PerplexityBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/perplexitybot): Perplexity. Surfaces and links websites in Perplexity's search results.
- [PetalBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/petalbot): Huawei. Crawls pages for Petal Search and Huawei Assistant.
- [Pinterestbot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/pinterestbot): Pinterest. Indexes pages behind Pins and keeps Pin details up to date.
- [Rogerbot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/rogerbot): Moz. Crawls a site for the site audits of a Moz Pro Campaign.
- [Screaming Frog SEO Spider](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/screaming-frog-seo-spider): Screaming Frog. Audits a site's technical SEO from the machine that runs it.
- [SemrushBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/semrushbot): Semrush. Collects web data for Semrush's SEO tools.
- [SeznamBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/seznambot): Seznam.cz. Crawls pages for Seznam, a Czech search engine.
- [Slackbot-LinkExpanding](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/slackbot-linkexpanding): Slack. Fetches a page's meta tags when someone posts its link in Slack.
- [Storebot-Google](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/storebot-google): Google. Crawls product and store pages for Google Shopping.
- [Twitterbot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/twitterbot): X. Fetches card markup when a link is shared on X.
- [YandexBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/yandexbot): Yandex. Yandex's main search indexing crawler.
- [Yeti](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/yeti): Naver. Crawls pages for Naver search in South Korea.
- [YouBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/youbot): You.com. Crawls and indexes pages for the You.com search engine.

## Use cases
- [All use cases](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/use-cases): The automated-abuse problems Centinel is built for.
- [Control what scrapers and AI crawlers can access](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/use-cases/scraping-and-ai-crawlers): Evaluate scraping and AI crawler protection: verify crawler identities, assess browser automation, and request a free audit of your site's exposed pages.
- [Detect automation around high-risk login attempts](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/use-cases/account-takeover): Detect credential-stuffing automation with browser and session evidence, and set a login policy you can review.
- [Detect card-testing automation in web checkout](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/use-cases/checkout-and-carding-fraud): Detect card-testing automation around checkout and apply a route-specific response before repeated attempts reach payment processing.
- [Detect automated sign-ups behind repeated promo claims](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/use-cases/promo-abuse-and-multi-accounting): Detect automated sign-ups used for promo abuse and apply a policy you can review. Centinel does not treat every new account as fraud.
- [Detect the scripts that trigger paid SMS verification codes](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/use-cases/sms-pumping): Detect SMS pumping automation on sign-up, login, and OTP routes, and challenge scripted code requests before your SMS provider sends and bills them.
- [Apply request-level policy to direct API traffic](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/use-cases/api-abuse): Evaluate direct API traffic with the request and session data your server integration passes to Centinel. Keep your existing API security controls.
- [Separate application-layer bot floods from volumetric DDoS](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/use-cases/ddos-and-traffic-floods): Evaluate application-layer bot traffic with automation evidence while retaining dedicated volumetric DDoS and availability protection.

## Industries
- [All industries](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/industries): Listing platforms and the automation that targets them.
- [Detect and limit automated abuse of marketplace listings and messages](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/industries/marketplaces): Bot protection for online marketplaces and classifieds: detect price scraping, fake seller accounts, and scripted bulk messaging without challenging every buyer.
- [Protect real estate listings, agent contacts, and inquiries from bots](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/industries/real-estate-and-proptech): Bot protection for real estate portals and proptech marketplaces: detect real estate scraping, agent-contact harvesting, fake accounts, and scripted inquiries.
- [Protect product drops, checkout, and customer accounts from bots](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/industries/retail-and-ecommerce): E-commerce bot protection: detect price scraping, inventory and sneaker bots, card testing, and credential stuffing without challenging every shopper.
- [Detect scalper bots and scripted buying at the ticket on-sale](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/industries/ticketing-and-live-events): Bot protection for ticketing: detect scalper bots, seat-spinning holds, and bulk fan accounts at the on-sale without putting every fan through a CAPTCHA.
- [Protect fares, seat inventory, and loyalty accounts from travel bots](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/industries/travel-and-airlines): Detect fare scraping, seat-spinning holds, and loyalty account takeover at airlines, hotels, and online travel agencies, while approved metasearch partners keep access.
- [Decide which AI crawlers and scrapers can read your content](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/industries/media-and-publishing): Centinel is bot protection for publishers and media sites: verify AI crawlers, detect scrapers that ignore robots.txt, and keep search indexing.
- [Detect scripted logins, sign-ups, and code requests at banks and fintechs](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/industries/financial-services): Detect credential stuffing, scripted account opening, card testing, and OTP abuse at banks and fintechs, while approved aggregators keep access.

## Guides
- [All guides](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog): Every Centinel guide on bot detection, crawler policy, and automated abuse.
- [Cloudflare Managed Challenge vs JavaScript Challenge](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/cloudflare-managed-challenge-vs-javascript-challenge): Cloudflare Managed Challenge vs JavaScript Challenge: how each WAF action works, how clearance behaves, and which to use on article, search, login and checkout routes.
- [Cloudflare API challenge: diagnose HTML instead of JSON](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/cloudflare-api-challenge-diagnose-html-instead-of-json): A JSON endpoint behind Cloudflare returns HTML? Read cf-mitigated, trace the Ray ID in Security Events, and scope a fix to the right product and clients.
- [Cloudflare bot score: set thresholds by route](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/cloudflare-bot-score-set-thresholds-by-route): Set Cloudflare bot score thresholds per route: public pages, login, checkout, APIs and automation. Score ranges, rule patterns, rollout and rollback criteria.
- [Cloudways Bot Protection Whitelist: Narrow IP Exceptions](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/cloudways-bot-protection-whitelist-narrow-ip-exceptions): Use the Cloudways Bot Protection whitelist as a last-step exception: prove which layer returned the 403, allow one trusted IP, test it, then remove it.
- [Wordfence bot protection: crawler limits and Googlebot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/wordfence-bot-protection-crawler-limits-and-googlebot): How Wordfence crawler and human page-view limits, 404 thresholds and throttle versus block work, why only verified Google crawlers get exempted, and where PHP limits end.
- [Barracuda Advanced Bot Protection: Licensing and Deployment](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/barracuda-advanced-bot-protection-licensing-and-deployment): A documentation-based guide to barracuda advanced bot protection: appliance WAF vs WAF-as-a-Service, what is licensed, and how to test it safely.
- [Cequence Bot Protection: Deployment and Policy Checks](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/cequence-bot-protection-deployment-and-policy-checks): Cequence bot protection evaluated from public evidence: what Defender with Istio and Envoy shows, which claims to attribute, and a test plan for your pilot.
- [Bytespider Bot Attack: Diagnose and Contain Crawler Load](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/bytespider-bot-attack-diagnose-and-contain-crawler-load): Seeing a Bytespider bot attack in your logs? Prove impact first, treat the user-agent as a claim, scope blocks narrowly, and confirm origin and readers recovered.
- [Cloudflare Bot Management Alternatives: Architecture First](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/cloudflare-bot-management-alternatives-architecture-first): Compare Cloudflare Bot Management alternatives by where the decision is made and what evidence it sees, plus four acceptance tests to run on any vendor.
- [Ecommerce Bot Protection: Prevent Inventory Hoarding](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/ecommerce-bot-protection-prevent-inventory-hoarding): Ecommerce bot protection for inventory hoarding: map where add-to-cart reserves stock, cap unpaid holds, and test how much stock sits held but unpaid.
- [reCAPTCHA vs Cloudflare Turnstile: Server-Side Checks](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/recaptcha-vs-cloudflare-turnstile-server-side-checks): A recaptcha vs cloudflare comparison from the endpoint's side: what each server response returns, which fields to check, token replay, and what to measure.
- [Netlify Bot Protection: Firewall Rules and Rate Limits](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/netlify-bot-protection-firewall-rules-and-rate-limits): Netlify bot protection explained: what firewall traffic rules and rate limits control, request order, deploy scope, log checks, and safe rollback for operators.
- [What is ClaudeBot? Anthropic's Crawler Explained](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-claudebot-anthropics-crawler-explained): What is ClaudeBot? Learn how Anthropic's training crawler differs from Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User, and how to verify it before you allow, challenge or block.
- [Fastly Bot Protection: Pre-cache and Post-cache Checks](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/fastly-bot-protection-pre-cache-and-post-cache-checks): Fastly bot protection explained: what runs before the cache, what runs after, and the cookie, caching and hostname details that break challenge rollouts.
- [Laravel Bot Protection: Rate Limits and Trusted Proxies](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/laravel-bot-protection-rate-limits-and-trusted-proxies): Laravel bot protection for Laravel 11+ and 13.x: named route limiters, trusted proxies in bootstrap/app.php, shared cache, and tests for 429s and forged headers.
- [WordPress Bot Protection: Login and XML-RPC Controls](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/wordpress-bot-protection-login-and-xml-rpc-controls): Implement effective WordPress bot protection across login, XML-RPC, and REST endpoints behind your CDN without locking out editorial teams or syndication.
- [HAProxy Bot Protection: Stick Tables and Rate Limits](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/haproxy-bot-protection-stick-tables-and-rate-limits): Build practical HAProxy bot protection with stick tables, sliding windows, and maps. Learn where layer 7 rate limiting ends and edge challenges begin.
- [Imperva Advanced Bot Protection: Controls and Limits](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/imperva-advanced-bot-protection-controls-and-limits): Evaluate Imperva Advanced Bot Protection confidence levels, crawler policies, and API limits. Learn what vendor docs omit and how to verify bot traffic.
- [Azure Bot Protection: Front Door WAF Rules and Safe Deployment](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/azure-bot-protection-front-door-waf-rules-and-safe-deployment): Deploy azure bot protection safely across Front Door and App Gateway. Learn Bot Manager 1.1 rule overrides, JS challenge limits, and safe detection rollout.
- [Akamai Bot Protection: Policies, Bot Scores, and Tests](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/akamai-bot-protection-policies-bot-scores-and-tests): Configure Akamai bot protection with confidence. Learn how bot scores work, tune policy thresholds by endpoint, and test defenses against modern scrapers.
- [AWS Bot Protection: WAF Bot Control Levels and Safe Deployment](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/aws-bot-protection-waf-bot-control-levels-and-safe-deployment): Deploy native AWS bot protection using WAF Bot Control. Learn the difference between Common and Targeted inspection, rule labels, and safe Count mode rollouts.
- [Vercel Bot Protection: Verified Bots, Rules and Challenge Limits](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/vercel-bot-protection-verified-bots-rules-and-challenge-limits): Evaluate Vercel bot protection across BotID, AI rulesets, and Attack Mode. Learn what native edge rules catch and where advanced automation slips past.
- [Nginx Bot Protection: Rate Limits, Real IPs and Safe Rollout](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/nginx-bot-protection-rate-limits-real-ips-and-safe-rollout): Deploy Nginx bot protection without breaking real traffic. Configure real IPs, tune limit_req burst and nodelay, and test with dry-run logging.
- [Shopify Bot Protection: Checkout Controls and Storefront Limits](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/shopify-bot-protection-checkout-controls-and-storefront-limits): Evaluate native Shopify bot protection across checkout and theme forms. See what native tools cover, where storefront gaps remain, and how to verify traffic.
- [Cloudflare Bot Protection Pricing: Enterprise Quote Checklist](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/cloudflare-bot-protection-pricing-enterprise-quote-checklist): Understand Cloudflare bot protection pricing across Pro, Business, and Enterprise tiers. Prepare your scope and quote questions before procurement talks.
- [Bot Mitigation for Publishers: Manage Unknown Crawlers at Edge](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/bot-mitigation-for-publishers-manage-unknown-crawlers-at-edge): Publisher bot mitigation cannot treat unknown crawlers like known threats. Learn how to govern gray-zone traffic at the edge with clear rules and expiry dates.
- [Form Bot Protection: Reduce Fake Leads Without Blocking Buyers](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/form-bot-protection-reduce-fake-leads-without-blocking-buyers): Stop fake form submissions without breaking buyer conversions. Learn how server-side form bot protection blocks bots while preserving sales leads.
- [Camoufox Paywall Audit: Test Publisher Access Controls](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/camoufox-paywall-audit-test-publisher-access-controls): Conduct a Camoufox paywall audit on your media property. Test subscriber access controls, separate bot detection from authorization, and capture evidence.
- [Bot False Positive Testing: Verify Visitors Before Blocking](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/bot-false-positive-testing-verify-visitors-before-blocking): Run structured bot false positive testing before tightening edge WAF rules. Protect real readers, search bots, and subscribers with this publisher test matrix.
- [Scraper Incident Response: Preserve Evidence Before Blocking](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/scraper-incident-response-preserve-evidence-before-blocking): Execute a scraper incident response that preserves logs and forensic signals before blocking bots. Learn how to verify crawlers and stop bot IP rotation.
- [Checkout Fraud Detection: Separate Bot Traffic from Payment Risk](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/checkout-fraud-detection-separate-bot-traffic-from-payment-risk): Checkout fraud detection fails when you conflate bots with payment risk. Learn how to separate edge automation defense from transaction scoring.
- [Price Scraping Protection: Test Controls on Product Pages](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/price-scraping-protection-test-controls-on-product-pages): Test price scraping protection across product pages before rollout. Map endpoints, design layered limits, and audit false positives on real traffic.
- [Residential Proxy Scraper Detection: How to Test Scraping Services](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/residential-proxy-scraper-detection-how-to-test-scraping-services): Evaluate residential proxy scraper detection across scraping services and real traffic. Test detection stacks without blocking legitimate residential users.
- [AI crawler policy for publishers: A newsroom access template](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/ai-crawler-policy-for-publishers-a-newsroom-access-template): Build an AI crawler policy for publishers across editorial, legal, and tech. Classify bots, verify IPs, and stop scrapers without breaking search traffic.
- [AI crawler costs: Build a business case from your own traffic logs](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/ai-crawler-costs-build-a-business-case-from-your-own-traffic-logs): Calculate your true AI crawler costs from raw server logs and cloud invoices. A worksheet guide covering origin bandwidth, compute spend, and engineering time.
- [AI browser agents: what a website can verify](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/ai-browser-agents): Agentic browsers for site owners: ChatGPT's cloud browser signs its requests, while Comet and Claude in Chrome arrive as the user's own browser.
- [What is card testing? Signs, costs and defenses](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-card-testing): Card testing is scripted checking of stolen card details through a merchant's checkout or add-card flow. How it works, the signs, and what stops it.
- [Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode vs. Bot Management](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/cloudflare-bot-fight-mode-vs-bot-management): What Cloudflare's Bot Fight Mode, Super Bot Fight Mode, and Enterprise Bot Management each do, where each one stops, and when to move to the next level.
- [Best bot management software: 10 tools compared](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/best-bot-management-software): Ten bot management tools compared by deployment model, client-side signals, mobile and API coverage, and fit. Sourced from each vendor's own documentation.
- [Pay per crawl explained: HTTP 402 and TollBit](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/pay-per-crawl-explained): Pay per crawl charges AI crawlers per request. How Cloudflare, TollBit, RSL and x402 work, and why it depends on knowing which crawler is asking.
- [Fake Googlebot: how to spot an impersonator](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/fake-googlebot): Any client can send a Googlebot user agent. Verify the IP with reverse and forward DNS or Google's published ranges, and avoid the Google Cloud trap.
- [What is ticket scalping? How scalper bots work](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-ticket-scalping): Ticket scalping is buying limited tickets to resell at a markup, today mostly by bot. How scalper bots beat purchase limits, and what the BOTS Act prohibits.
- [What is price scraping? How to spot it in logs](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-price-scraping): Price scraping is the automated collection of prices from product, listing, or fare pages. See who runs it, how it shows up in logs, and which responses fit.
- [What is Stagehand? The AI browser automation SDK](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-stagehand): Stagehand is Browserbase's open-source SDK for driving Chromium with natural-language steps. How it works, where it runs, and what a target site can see.
- [What is nodriver? Python CDP automation explained](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-nodriver): nodriver is an async Python library that drives Chrome over the DevTools Protocol without Selenium or WebDriver. What it changes and what gives it away.
- [What is Crawl4AI? The open-source AI crawler](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-crawl4ai): Crawl4AI is an open-source Python crawler that turns web pages into Markdown for LLMs. What it can change, what your site sees, and how to assess it.
- [Fake Googlebot and AI crawlers: 2026 data](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/fake-crawler-report): On the typical news site, 1 in 7 requests claiming to be Googlebot failed verification, and 84% of GPTBot claims were fake. Data, method and CSV download.
- [How to respond to a layer 7 bot attack](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/respond-to-layer-7-bot-attacks): Contain an application-layer bot flood by finding the exhausted resource, narrowing traffic controls, and checking recovery. Includes an incident worksheet.
- [How to detect cache-busting bots](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/detect-cache-busting-bots): Investigate query-string variation, falling cache hits, and rising origin work. Review cache keys safely without merging meaningfully different responses.
- [Bot traffic or traffic spike? How to tell](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/bot-traffic-vs-traffic-spike): Compare traffic surges with request behavior, route cost, and real workflow completion. Avoid blocking a flash crowd or overlooking a bot-driven overload.
- [GraphQL rate limiting for expensive queries](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/prevent-graphql-abuse): Bound GraphQL query depth, breadth, pagination, and cost. Learn why HTTP request limits alone miss expensive operations.
- [How to detect bot abuse on APIs](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/detect-api-bot-abuse): Investigate API automation using credentials, routes, resource use, and outcomes. Distinguish approved clients from abusive requests.
- [API rate limiting for bot protection](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/api-rate-limiting-for-bot-protection): Choose API rate limits around client identity, route cost, bursts, and retries. Avoid one global rule that blocks users but misses expensive abuse.
- [How to prevent automated promo-code abuse](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/prevent-promo-code-abuse): Protect promotion eligibility and redemption from bots. Review repeated claims, concurrent requests, and retry handling without relying on IP alone.
- [Fake accounts: how to detect automated signups](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/detect-automated-account-creation): Fake accounts are registered in bulk, usually by scripts, for spam, fake reviews, or repeated sign-up credits. How to detect them from signup to first use.
- [Card testing: how to prevent carding attacks](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/how-to-prevent-carding-attacks): Card testing, or carding, uses scripts to check stolen card details against payment and card-setup flows. How to spot it and stop it before the provider call.
- [How to prevent password-reset flooding and abuse](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/prevent-password-reset-abuse): Protect recovery requests from automated flooding. Bound email delivery, retries, and token handling without letting attackers lock legitimate users out.
- [How to prevent OTP request abuse and SMS pumping](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/prevent-otp-request-abuse): Control automated one-time-code requests before delivery. Review resend budgets, destination patterns, and outcomes without blocking legitimate recovery.
- [How to prevent account enumeration](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/prevent-account-enumeration): Find account-existence leaks in login, signup, and password recovery. Review messages, status codes, and timing while keeping recovery usable.
- [How to prevent account takeover](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/how-to-prevent-account-takeover): Protect login, password recovery, and account changes with layered controls. Learn where bot protection helps and which identity checks remain essential.
- [Credential stuffing: what it is, how to detect it](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/detect-credential-stuffing): Credential stuffing is automated login testing with username and password pairs stolen from other sites. How it differs from brute force and how to detect it.
- [How to investigate bot-detection false positives](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/investigate-bot-detection-false-positives): Trace a legitimate user's block to the decision that caused it. Separate classification errors, policy mistakes, and integration failures.
- [How to identify bot traffic in Google Analytics 4](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/how-to-identify-bot-traffic-in-google-analytics): Spot bot traffic in GA4: rule out collection mistakes, build a slice of suspicious sessions, and confirm it against request logs before you block anything.
- [CAPTCHA loop: why it repeats and how to fix it](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/fix-bot-challenge-loops): A CAPTCHA challenge is a check a site runs before it lets a request through. Why visitors get stuck in repeat challenges, and how to find the failing step.
- [CAPTCHA alternatives for your workflow](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/captcha-alternatives): Compare non-interactive checks, proof of work, authentication, and workflow controls. Choose a CAPTCHA alternative by what it protects and how users recover.
- [How to run a bot-protection proof of concept](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/bot-protection-proof-of-concept): Build a buyer-owned bot-protection evaluation with clear workflows, labeled traffic, and enforcement checks. Includes a practical scorecard.
- [How to protect site search from bot abuse](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/protect-site-search-from-bots): Investigate automated search queries, deep pagination, and expensive filters. Set search-specific budgets while preserving useful search and autocomplete.
- [Protect data-export endpoints from abuse](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/protect-data-exports-from-abuse): Review export permissions, queue admission, result delivery, and signed downloads. Bound automated bulk extraction without disrupting approved data exports.
- [How to prevent authenticated scraping](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/prevent-authenticated-scraping): Control automated extraction by signed-in users. Review account permissions, resource budgets, exports, and approved integrations.
- [How to prevent web scraping](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/how-to-prevent-web-scraping): Choose scraping controls by route: access checks, rate limits, crawler rules, and bot detection. Use a control matrix to test failures and roll back safely.
- [How to detect low-and-slow web scraping](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/detect-low-and-slow-scraping): Find scraping that stays under short rate limits by comparing resource coverage, account activity, and extraction over a longer window than a rate chart.
- [How to audit AI crawler traffic on your website](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/audit-ai-crawler-traffic): Build a crawler inventory from request logs. Separate claimed names, verified operators, resource use, and policy outcomes before changing crawler access.
- [What is an antidetect browser?](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-an-antidetect-browser): An antidetect browser changes the browser characteristics a site can observe. Learn how profiles work, which inconsistencies matter, and how to respond.
- [How to detect bots using residential proxies](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/detect-bots-using-residential-proxies): Detect bots behind residential proxies using trusted source data, client consistency, and workflow evidence. Choose scoped controls without blocking whole ISPs.
- [What is Zyte API? Scraping modes and detection](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-zyte): Zyte API fetches raw HTTP, runs managed browsers and extracts structured data. What each mode looks like to a target site, and how to assess it.
- [Ulixee Hero: the scraping browser and detection](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-ulixee-hero): Ulixee Hero is a Chrome-based scraping browser that emulates an ordinary browser. What its emulation covers and how Centinel detected it in a 2026 test.
- [Playwright Stealth: what it patches and misses](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-playwright-stealth): playwright-stealth hides navigator.webdriver and other simple automation tells. What the Python package patches, what it cannot hide, how sites spot it.
- [Kernel browser (kernel.sh): cloud Chromium](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-kernel-sh): Kernel runs on-demand cloud Chromium for web agents. How it works, what its stealth mode changes, and how Centinel detected it in a September 2026 test.
- [Camoufox in 2026: does it beat bot detection?](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-camoufox): Camoufox is a Firefox fork that spoofs fingerprints in C++. What it changes, the leaks its docs admit, and how Centinel detected it in a 2026 test.
- [What is Firecrawl? How it scrapes and is detected](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-firecrawl): Firecrawl turns web pages into Markdown or structured data for AI agents. How it fetches, what your site sees, and how Centinel detected it in a 2026 test.
- [What is Browserbase? Cloud browsers for AI agents](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-browserbase): Browserbase rents remote Chromium sessions to AI agents over an API. How sessions work, what a target site sees, and how Centinel detected it in a 2026 test.
- [Browser Use: how the AI browser agent gets caught](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-browser-use): Browser Use lets a language model drive a real browser. How the agent works, what your logs see, and how Centinel detected it in a September 2026 test.
- [Why WAF rules can miss browser-like crawlers](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/why-your-waf-cant-see-them): Learn where request rules end, where session evidence can help, and how to test the bot controls enabled in your WAF without relying on category claims.
- [What is agentic traffic? AI agents explained](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-ai-agent-traffic): Agentic traffic comes from software that picks and performs steps toward a user's goal. How it differs from crawlers and fetchers, and how to measure it.
- [How to control AI agent access](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/how-to-control-ai-agent-access): Build a practical access policy for AI crawlers and agents with a resource matrix, explicit identity states, bounded responses, and tested failure behavior.
- [Verify AI crawlers and agents: spot fake GPTBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/how-to-verify-ai-agents): Check whether a request claiming to be GPTBot, ClaudeBot or another AI agent is real, using published IP ranges, reverse DNS or signed requests.
- [Interstitial challenge pages for protection](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/interstitial-page-content-protection): Decide when an interstitial challenge fits a protected route, which failure modes to handle, and how to measure the result before broad rollout.
- [Automated browser detection: evidence and actions](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/detect-browser-automation): Detect Playwright, Selenium and other automated browsers with request, browser and session evidence, then choose when to observe, challenge or block.
- [Patched Chromium browsers explained](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/patched-chromium-browsers): Learn what patched Chromium means, which automation signals a patch can change, and how to test browser-automation detection without relying on one property.
- [TLS fingerprinting explained: JA3 vs JA4](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/tls-fingerprinting-explained): A JA3 or JA4 fingerprint summarizes a TLS ClientHello. How each is built, how to read and capture one, and why a TLS fingerprint alone never proves a bot.
- [GPTBot vs ClaudeBot vs Bytespider compared](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/gptbot-vs-claudebot-vs-bytespider): Compare GPTBot, ClaudeBot and Bytespider: each operator's stated purpose, robots.txt guidance, published IP ranges, and how to check a claim.
- [robots.txt for AI bots: tokens and examples](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/robots-txt-ai-bots-guide): Copy-ready robots.txt rules for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended and other AI crawler tokens, how to test them, and why robots.txt cannot stop fakes.
- [How to block AI crawlers and verify the block](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/how-to-block-ai-crawlers): Block GPTBot, ClaudeBot and other AI crawlers: robots.txt rules by purpose, a verified request rule for copied names, and two curl checks to test it.
- [What is web scraping?](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-web-scraping): Understand how web scraping works, how it differs from crawling and browser automation, and how to build a resource-specific response.
- [What is an AI crawler? Types and examples](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/what-is-an-ai-crawler): AI crawlers collect web content for model development, AI search and retrieval. How they work, the main operators' crawlers, and what your logs can show.

# Bot directory

55 crawlers and fetchers that reach public websites: who runs each one, what it does, and its robots.txt token. Last checked 2026-10-10.

## AI training and dataset crawlers

Crawl the web for content that may be used to train models or to build a reusable dataset.

| Bot | Operator | What it does | robots.txt token |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Amazonbot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/amazonbot) | Amazon | Crawls to improve Amazon products; may be used to train Amazon AI models. | `Amazonbot` |
| [CCBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/ccbot) | Common Crawl | Builds Common Crawl's open web archive, free for anyone to reuse. | `CCBot` |
| [ClaudeBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/claudebot) | Anthropic | Collects web content that could contribute to Claude model training. | `ClaudeBot` |
| [GPTBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/gptbot) | OpenAI | Crawls content that may be used to train OpenAI's foundation models. | `GPTBot` |
| [Meta-ExternalAgent](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/meta-externalagent) | Meta | Crawls for training AI models or improving Meta products. | `meta-externalagent` |

## AI search crawlers

Index pages so an AI assistant can find, cite and link them in its answers.

| Bot | Operator | What it does | robots.txt token |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Claude-SearchBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/claude-searchbot) | Anthropic | Indexes pages to improve Claude's search results. | `Claude-SearchBot` |
| [DuckAssistBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/duckassistbot) | DuckDuckGo | Crawls in real time to support DuckDuckGo's AI-assisted answers. | `DuckAssistBot` |
| [Meta-WebIndexer](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/meta-webindexer) | Meta | Crawls pages to improve the search results of Meta AI. | `meta-webindexer` |
| [MistralAI-Index](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/mistralai-index) | Mistral AI | Indexes pages for Mistral search. | `MistralAI-Index` |
| [OAI-SearchBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/oai-searchbot) | OpenAI | Surfaces websites in ChatGPT's search features. | `OAI-SearchBot` |
| [PerplexityBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/perplexitybot) | Perplexity | Surfaces and links websites in Perplexity's search results. | `PerplexityBot` |

## AI user-triggered fetchers

Fetch a page because a person asked an assistant to. Several operators say robots.txt may not apply.

| Bot | Operator | What it does | robots.txt token |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [ChatGPT-User](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/chatgpt-user) | OpenAI | Visits a page when a ChatGPT or Custom GPT user's request needs it. | `ChatGPT-User` |
| [Claude-User](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/claude-user) | Anthropic | Fetches a page when a Claude user's question needs it. | `Claude-User` |
| [Meta-ExternalFetcher](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/meta-externalfetcher) | Meta | Fetches individual links on behalf of Meta product users. | `meta-externalfetcher` |
| [MistralAI-User](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/mistralai-user) | Mistral AI | Fetches a page when a Mistral user's action needs it. | `MistralAI-User` |
| [Perplexity-User](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/perplexity-user) | Perplexity | Fetches a page when a Perplexity user's request needs it. | `Perplexity-User` |

## AI robots.txt control tokens

Names you write in robots.txt to control how an operator uses your content for AI. No crawler sends them as a user agent.

| Bot | Operator | What it does | robots.txt token |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Applebot-Extended](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/applebot-extended) | Apple | A robots.txt token that opts content out of Apple model training. | `Applebot-Extended` |
| [Google-Extended](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/google-extended) | Google | A robots.txt token that controls Gemini training and grounding use. | `Google-Extended` |

## Search engine crawlers

Build the indexes behind web search results.

| Bot | Operator | What it does | robots.txt token |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| [Applebot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/applebot) | Apple | Crawls pages for Spotlight, Siri and Safari search features. | `Applebot` |
| [Baiduspider](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/baiduspider) | Baidu | Crawls pages for Baidu search. | `Baiduspider` |
| [Bingbot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/bingbot) | Microsoft | Crawls pages for Bing search. | `bingbot` |
| [Diffbot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/diffbot) | Diffbot | Crawls the web for the Diffbot Knowledge Graph and Diffbot's web search services. | `Diffbot` |
| [DuckDuckBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/duckduckbot) | DuckDuckGo | Crawls pages for DuckDuckGo search. | `DuckDuckBot` |
| [Googlebot-Image](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/googlebot-image) | Google | Crawls images for Google Images and image features in Search. | `Googlebot-Image` |
| [Googlebot-News](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/googlebot-news) | Google | Controls whether your pages appear in Google News. | `Googlebot-News` |
| [Googlebot-Video](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/googlebot-video) | Google | Crawls video for the video features of Google Search. | `Googlebot-Video` |
| [Googlebot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/googlebot) | Google | Crawls pages for Google Search, Images, Video, News and Discover. | `Googlebot` |
| [Kagibot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/kagibot) | Kagi | Crawls pages for the Kagi search engine. | `Kagibot` |
| [PetalBot](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/petalbot) | Huawei | Crawls pages for Petal Search and Huawei Assistant. | `PetalBot` |

## How to verify a request from Google

- AdsBot-Google and Mediapartners-Google: Run a reverse DNS lookup on the source IP and check that the name ends in google.com (Google uses rate-limited-proxy-….google.com for special-case crawlers), then run a forward lookup on that name and confirm it returns the same IP. Or check the IP against Google's special-case crawler ranges. https://developers.google.com/static/crawling/ipranges/special-crawlers.json
- Google-CloudVertexBot, Google-InspectionTool, Googlebot-Image, Googlebot-Video, Googlebot, GoogleOther and Storebot-Google: Run a reverse DNS lookup on the source IP and check that the name ends in googlebot.com (Google uses crawl-….googlebot.com and geo-crawl-….geo.googlebot.com), then run a forward lookup on that name and confirm it returns the same IP. Or check the IP against Google's common crawler ranges. A googleusercontent.com name does not count: any Google Cloud virtual machine can have one. https://developers.google.com/static/crawling/ipranges/common-crawlers.json
- Google-Extended: There is nothing to verify: no Google crawler sends Google-Extended as its user agent. A request that does is not from Google.
- Googlebot-News: No request carries Googlebot-News as its user agent. The crawl comes from Googlebot, so verify it as Googlebot: run a reverse DNS lookup on the source IP, check that the name ends in googlebot.com, then run a forward lookup on that name and confirm it returns the same IP. Or check the IP against Google's common crawler ranges. https://developers.google.com/static/crawling/ipranges/common-crawlers.json

# What is 360Spider?

360Spider is the web search crawler of 360 Search (so.com). 360 Search uses separate user agents for its other products: 360Spider-Image for image search and 360Spider-Video for video search. Its documentation is in Chinese.

- Operator: 360 Search
- Purpose: Crawls pages for the web search of 360 Search (so.com).
- robots.txt token: `360Spider`
- Example user agent: `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/140.0.0.0 Safari/537.36 Edg/140.0.0.0; 360Spider`
- How to verify: 360 Search lists the IP segments of its spider on its help page and says to use that list, because the spider does not currently support a reverse DNS lookup. Compare the source IP with the segments on the page.
- Operator documentation: [https://www.so.com/help/spider_ip.html](https://www.so.com/help/spider_ip.html)
- Last verified: 2026-10-10

## How often is 360Spider impersonated?

Too few organisations saw requests claiming to be 360Spider in the measurement window to publish a share.

This directory measures requests between 14 July 2026 and 10 October 2026. The [fake crawler report](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/fake-crawler-report) covers its own, earlier window (late June to 21 September 2026), so its figures differ from the ones here. Read it for the method.

## Should you block 360Spider?

- Allow it if: you have visitors who search with 360 Search.
- Block it if: you have no audience in China and the crawl adds load.
- What blocking changes: 360 Search warns site owners not to block its spider by mistake, because that causes indexing or crawling problems in 360 Search.

To block it, add this group to your robots.txt. 360 Search says it supports the main commands of the robots protocol: User-agent, Allow and Disallow.

```
User-agent: 360Spider
Disallow: /
```

robots.txt only asks. It does nothing against a client that ignores it or only pretends to be 360Spider. Stopping those takes verification at your edge.

# What is AdsBot-Google?

AdsBot-Google is the crawler Google Ads uses to check the quality of web pages used as ad landing pages. It is one of Google's special-case crawlers.

- Operator: [Google](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/bots/operator/google)
- Purpose: Checks the quality of ad landing pages for Google Ads.
- robots.txt token: `AdsBot-Google`
- Example user agent: `AdsBot-Google (+http://www.google.com/adsbot.html)`
- How to verify: Run a reverse DNS lookup on the source IP and check that the name ends in google.com (Google uses rate-limited-proxy-….google.com for special-case crawlers), then run a forward lookup on that name and confirm it returns the same IP. Or check the IP against Google's special-case crawler ranges.
- Reverse DNS: google.com
- IP ranges: [https://developers.google.com/static/crawling/ipranges/special-crawlers.json](https://developers.google.com/static/crawling/ipranges/special-crawlers.json)
- Operator documentation: [https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/google-special-case-crawlers](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/google-special-case-crawlers)
- Last verified: 2026-09-30

## How often is AdsBot-Google impersonated?

For the median organisation, under 1% of requests claiming to be AdsBot-Google failed verification.

Measured between 14 July 2026 and 10 October 2026 across organisations protected by Centinel. We only publish a share when at least five organisations each saw enough of these requests. Pooled across all of their requests, the share was under 1%: a few large organisations carry most of the traffic, so the median organisation is the better guide to what yours will see.

This directory measures requests between 14 July 2026 and 10 October 2026. The [fake crawler report](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/fake-crawler-report) covers its own, earlier window (late June to 21 September 2026), so its figures differ from the ones here. Read it for the method.

## Should you block AdsBot-Google?

- Allow it if: you run Google Ads that point to this site.
- Block it if: you do not advertise with Google. Remember that User-agent: * does not cover it.
- What blocking changes: Google Ads can no longer check your landing pages, which can affect ads that point to them.

To block it, add this group to your robots.txt. Google says AdsBot ignores the global User-agent: * group. A rule only applies if it names AdsBot-Google.

```
User-agent: AdsBot-Google
Disallow: /
```

# What is Googlebot?

Googlebot is Google's main search crawler. Google says rules addressed to Googlebot affect Google Search, including Discover and all Search features, and other products such as Google Images, Google Video and Google News.

Or check the IP against Google's common crawler ranges. A googleusercontent.com name does not count: any Google Cloud virtual machine can have one.

## Should you block Googlebot?

- Allow it if: you want to appear in Google Search. This is nearly every public site.
- Block it if: a section should never appear in Google, such as internal search results. Block the path, not the crawler.

User-agent: Googlebot

# Cloudflare Managed Challenge vs JavaScript Challenge

Cloudflare Managed Challenge vs JavaScript Challenge: how each WAF action works, how clearance behaves, and which to use on article, search, login and checkout routes.

By Centinel Analytica. Published 2026-11-09.

Use Managed Challenge as the default action on browser page routes, and reserve the JavaScript (non-interactive) challenge for routes where you never want a visitor to see or do anything. Managed Challenge lets Cloudflare pick the check per request. The JavaScript Challenge always runs a non-interactive check. Neither pass proves the visitor is human.

This post is a route-by-route guide for platform, DevOps and security engineers who write Cloudflare WAF rules for article pages, search, login and checkout. It also keeps three easily confused things apart: the challenge actions, JavaScript Detections and the Turnstile widget. Centinel Analytica is bot and AI crawler protection that tells real visitors from scrapers that look like them and applies allow, challenge or block policy through your existing CDN or edge. It sits beside Cloudflare and does not replace it. The last section covers where a challenge pass stops and that layer starts.

## Managed Challenge vs JavaScript Challenge: the short answer

Managed Challenge is adaptive and JavaScript Challenge is fixed. With a Managed Challenge, Cloudflare chooses the type of check based on the characteristics of the request, so one visitor may pass silently while another gets an interaction. The JavaScript Challenge, which Cloudflare's docs call a Non-Interactive Challenge, runs a browser-side check and never asks the visitor to act ([Cloudflare Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/challenge-types/challenge-pages/)).

A third action, Interactive Challenge, always requires the visitor to interact. Cloudflare generally recommends Managed Challenge over it.

Pick by what you can tolerate. If a stuck visitor on a revenue route costs you more than a missed bot, choose the action that never asks for interaction. If you'd rather let Cloudflare escalate when signals look weak, choose Managed. Don't treat any of these as a verdict on humanity. A pass means the browser satisfied a client-side check, nothing more.

## What each challenge action does on a browser page route

All three actions are interstitial Challenge Pages: a full-page screen that appears before the visitor reaches the destination URL and acts as a gate while Cloudflare verifies the request ([Cloudflare Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/challenge-types/challenge-pages/)). They interrupt the request flow by returning a full HTML page for the browser to render and solve. That's why they suit browser page routes and are a poor fit for API calls or fetch requests that expect JSON.

**Non-Interactive (JavaScript) Challenge.** Cloudflare decides whether the visitor is automated from the limited information it can gather in the browser. The visitor sees a brief wait screen and nothing to click. Use it where friction must stay near zero.

**Managed Challenge.** Cloudflare dynamically chooses the appropriate challenge type for the visitor. In practice that means a non-interactive check when signals are good and an interactive step when they aren't. You hand the escalation decision to Cloudflare.

**Interactive Challenge.** The visitor must interact to pass. It's the most visible action and the one most likely to lose a real user mid-task.

If a challenge loops or traps real users, use the troubleshooting guides on this blog instead of re-deriving incident steps here.

## Comparison table: Managed, JavaScript and Interactive challenge actions

| Criterion | Managed Challenge | JavaScript (Non-Interactive) Challenge | Interactive Challenge |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Who picks the check | Cloudflare, per request | Fixed: non-interactive | Fixed: interactive |
| Visitor action required | Sometimes | Never | Always |
| Cloudflare's stated preference | Recommended for most WAF rules | Available when you need zero interaction | Generally not recommended over Managed |
| Challenge clearance level granted | Medium | Low | High |
| Bypasses on later requests | Managed and Non-Interactive | Non-Interactive only | Interactive, Managed and Non-Interactive |
| Best fit | Most browser page routes | Routes where any visible step hurts | Narrow cases where you want a deliberate step |

The clearance rows come from Cloudflare's clearance model, covered next. Treat the "best fit" row as a starting point for your own testing, not a universal ranking. The actions aren't ordered by security strength, and no row guarantees a bot is stopped.

## Clearance hierarchy: Challenge clearance, Precursor clearance and Challenge Passage

A successful challenge writes a `cf_clearance` cookie so the visitor isn't challenged again on every request ([Cloudflare Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-challenges/concepts/clearance/)). Two different mechanisms govern whether that clearance holds, and they're easy to conflate.

**Challenge clearance** is granted when a visitor completes a challenge. Its level follows the challenge passed:





A lower clearance doesn't bypass a higher challenge. If a visitor with low clearance hits a rule that issues a Managed Challenge, they're challenged again, and solving the higher one replaces the earlier clearance.

**Challenge Passage** is the zone-level setting for how long Challenge clearance normally lasts. The default is 30 minutes, and Cloudflare suggests staying in a range around 15 to 45 minutes.

**Precursor clearance** is separate. It's a continuously updated assessment of session behavior. In Armed mode, Precursor re-evaluates clearance throughout a visitor's session and can reduce or invalidate effective clearance, triggering a new challenge before the cookie's Challenge Passage time runs out. In Monitor mode it doesn't change Challenge clearance.

The practical rule: a cookie that hasn't expired doesn't guarantee an uninterrupted visit. When you measure repeat challenges, check whether Precursor is in Armed mode before blaming your Challenge Passage value.

## Not the same thing: JavaScript Detections and the Turnstile widget

Three Cloudflare features carry "JavaScript" or "challenge" in their description, and they're different tools.

The **JavaScript Challenge action** is a WAF rule action that serves a Challenge Page and gates the request until the check passes.

**JavaScript Detections** is, per Cloudflare, a type of challenge separate from Challenge Pages and Turnstile. Its limits matter on page routes. The first request from a new client generally has no detection data, a Content Security Policy can interfere with the injected script, and it strips ETags from HTML responses where it's injected. It isn't injected if your origin sends `Cache-Control: no-transform`.

The **Turnstile widget** is a component you embed in a page, such as a login form. It can also use pre-clearance, which issues `cf_clearance` cookies so a visitor who passed the widget isn't challenged again by WAF rules on the same zone. The widget hostname must match the zone with the WAF rules, and the cookie lasts for the zone's Challenge Passage value.

For a deeper comparison of widget-style checks, see [reCAPTCHA vs Cloudflare Turnstile: server-side checks](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/recaptcha-vs-cloudflare-turnstile-server-side-checks).

## Which action for which browser route: article, search, login and checkout examples

These are decision examples, not measured results. Test each on a small slice before enforcing.

**Article pages.** The goal is usually to slow bulk retrieval without hurting readers arriving from search or social. Start with Managed Challenge scoped to suspicious signals rather than all traffic, so most readers never see a step. Avoid Interactive here. A reader who bounces rarely returns.

**Search and listing pages.** These are common scraping targets and also high-volume for real users. A JavaScript Challenge fits when you want a zero-interaction gate on a narrow rule, for example a burst of requests to a search path. Keep the rule scoped by path and rate so ordinary browsing is untouched.

**Login.** Prefer Managed Challenge on the page that serves the form. If you want the check inside the page rather than as an interstitial, consider a Turnstile widget with pre-clearance on the form itself. Interstitials don't suit the XHR calls a single-page login makes, so keep the challenge on the page load.

**Checkout.** Friction has a direct revenue cost, so default to the least visible action that your tests show is adequate. A non-interactive check on the cart-to-checkout transition is a reasonable first trial. Escalate to Managed only if you see abuse in your own logs. See [ecommerce bot protection: prevent inventory hoarding](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/ecommerce-bot-protection-prevent-inventory-hoarding) for the abuse patterns that justify it.

In every case, mind clearance. If a user passes a low-clearance JavaScript Challenge and a later rule issues a Managed Challenge, they're challenged again. Align the actions you use across a user journey so one route doesn't undo the other.

## Measure challenge completion and user impact

Enforcement without measurement just moves the problem. Before you switch a rule from log to challenge, decide what you'll compare.

1. **Issued vs solved.** For each rule, count challenges issued and challenges solved. A low solve rate on a route real users depend on is a signal to loosen the action or narrow the rule.
2. **Funnel completion on the protected route.** Track the share of sessions that reach the next step, such as search to article, login form to authenticated session, cart to order. Compare before and after on the same segment.
3. **Repeat challenges per session.** If the same session is challenged more than once, check clearance level mismatches across rules and whether Precursor is Armed.
4. **Support contacts and abandonment.** Tag complaints that mention verification screens.
5. **Record legitimate completions as well as suspicious activity.** Blocking more sessions isn't success if intended users can no longer finish the workflow.

Run the rule in a log or low-scope mode first, change one variable at a time, and keep a rollback. For the cost side of Cloudflare's bot tooling, the [Cloudflare bot protection pricing checklist](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/cloudflare-bot-protection-pricing-enterprise-quote-checklist) lists what to ask for in an enterprise quote.

## Where a challenge pass stops and Centinel starts

A challenge pass is evidence that a browser completed a client-side check at one moment. It isn't proof of a human, and it says nothing about what the session does afterward. Headless and scripted browsers are built to run JavaScript, so a scraper that renders pages can satisfy a non-interactive action and still extract your content.

That gap is where a second layer helps. Centinel tells real visitors from scrapers and applies allow, challenge or block policy through your existing CDN or edge. It works alongside Cloudflare, CloudFront, Akamai and Fastly, and your CDN or WAF stays in place. Published research from the team found that on a typical news site, 84% of requests claiming to be GPTBot were fake. A user-agent rule or a single challenge pass won't settle that kind of traffic.

In practice: keep your Cloudflare challenge actions for the routes above, and use Centinel to decide which sessions deserve a challenge, an allow or a block. For architecture-level options, see [Cloudflare Bot Management alternatives: architecture first](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/blog/cloudflare-bot-management-alternatives-architecture-first).

## Default to Managed, gate quietly where you must, and add a layer that judges the session

Use Managed Challenge on most browser page routes, a JavaScript (non-interactive) Challenge where any visible step costs you users, and Interactive only on purpose. Keep clearance levels consistent across a journey, check whether Precursor is Armed, and measure issued versus solved before enforcing. Then accept that no pass proves a human. To see how much scraper and fake-crawler traffic gets through your current Cloudflare setup, [book a demo with Centinel Analytica](https://www.centinelanalytica.com/book-a-demo).


## Frequently asked questions

### What is the difference between Cloudflare Managed Challenge and JavaScript Challenge?

Managed Challenge lets Cloudflare choose the check per request, so some visitors pass silently and others get an interaction. Cloudflare classifies the JavaScript Challenge as a Non-Interactive Challenge, though a check can fail and require further action. Cloudflare recommends Managed for most WAF rules. Centinel Analytica adds a layer beside Cloudflare to tell real visitors from scrapers.

### Does passing a Cloudflare challenge prove the visitor is human?

No. A pass means the browser satisfied a client-side check and earned a cf_clearance cookie, which Cloudflare documentation describes as proof that the visitor is a verified human. Scripted browsers can run JavaScript. Centinel Analytica tells real visitors from scrapers that look like them.

### Is the JavaScript Challenge the same as JavaScript Detections?

No. The JavaScript Challenge is a challenge type, while WAF rules can use the Challenge action to serve an interstitial Challenge Page. JavaScript Detections is a separate feature that injects an invisible script into your pages and is enforced through a WAF field. Turnstile is a third thing, an embeddable widget. Centinel Analytica works beside all of them at your CDN or edge.

### How does Cloudflare know I'm not a bot?

Cloudflare evaluates signals from the request and the browser, and may run a non-interactive or interactive check depending on the action. In relevant challenge clearance flows, passing issues a cf_clearance cookie. Precursor can later re-evaluate the session in Armed mode. No signal is a proof of humanity, which is why teams add Centinel Analytica as a second layer.
